sections.html:
Bacon County sits in southeast Georgia with Alma as the seat, and it is mostly open country. Around 11,070 people call it home, slightly fewer than the 11,140 counted in 2020, so you will not find crowds. A typical listing is a house on a country lot, often with a well, a septic tank and room for outbuildings.

Alma is the lone city. Rockingham, Coffee and Sessoms are small outlying communities, so many owners hold land well outside town.

sections.h2: Home values and what buyers compare
sections.html:
Home prices rank near the bottom statewide. Owners occupy 68.6% of the housing.

Housing units (July 2025)4,863

Residents who did not move in the past year93.3%

Only fourteen permits were issued in all of 2025, so hardly any new houses are going up and a shopper will compare yours with older stock. Turnover is slow too. Price your place against recent closings close by, not against a statewide average.

In 2020, 4,807 housing units existed here and about 11.6% were vacant, while 31.7% of occupied units were rentals. Empty houses mean your listing may compete with several that need work.

Both the tax commissioner and the assessors are in the Bacon County Government Building, 502 West 12th Street, Suite 101, Alma, GA 31510. Call 912-632-5614 during office hours, 9:00 am to 5:00 pm. The commissioner's website has more.

  • Suite 101, tax commissioner: bills, what you owe, liens, mobile home permits
  • Suite 101, tax assessors: your value, returns, exemptions, appeals
  • Suite 200, Clerk of Superior Court: deed copies

Look up a parcel on qPublic. The website is general information only and state law wins if the two differ, so phone the office whenever the exact amount matters.

November 15 is the usual due date, with bills mailed at least two months ahead. That date can shift in a given year, so follow what your own bill says.

Two installments are available, but any balance left after the deadline keeps growing. A check in the mail is on time if postmarked by the due date, and weekends and holidays push the date to the next business day. Look for the drop box at the right edge of the front lot. Paying by card costs an extra 2.75% to the processor, at least $2.00.

  • Interest is added each month at prime plus three percentage points
  • A 5% penalty hits at the 120-day mark, repeats at each further 120 days, and caps at 20%
  • Homesteaded parcels billed under $500 are spared the penalty
  • Mobile homes have their own April 1 due date, with a 10% penalty

sections.h2: Can a tax lien follow a Bacon County sale?
sections.html:
Yes, if the bill is still open. A month after the bill goes unpaid, the office may record a FiFa, a lien filed with the Clerk of Superior Court on the General Execution Docket. The county cautions that it can follow you on a credit file for seven years or more. Delinquent notices are sent only now and then, so phone for today's figure before paying.

Georgia puts the lien on the person who held title on January 1. To shift it to your buyer, take the signed closing statement to Suite 101 inside 90 days of the due date. If a bill finds you after you have sold, pass it along to the buyer.

  1. Get a written payoff figure from Suite 101.
  2. Let the title company deduct it at closing.
  3. Save your settlement statement.

Count 45 days from the date on your assessment notice. Hand the assessors a written dispute on the standard state form, giving one reason: taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption.

Your filing also picks the route the case takes. Pick the Board of Equalization and the assessors get a chance to revise the figure, which opens 30 days to answer any amended notice. A dispute that survives goes to a board hearing, then possibly Superior Court. Non-homestead real estate above a set value can use a hearing officer instead. Arbitration needs a certified appraisal and settles the question for good.

You can also state your own value on a return filed between January 1 and April 1. Real estate returns roll forward without refiling. Personal property needs a fresh return each year.

sections.h2: Exemptions that can lower the bill
sections.html:
Homestead matters most for owner-occupants. A statewide baseline applies, Bacon County layers its own exemptions on top, and the bigger of the two is what you get. You must own and occupy the house on January 1, and your form has to be in the assessors' hands by April 1 in your first year. After approval it renews each year without refiling.

  • Tax deferral for owners 62 and older with household income of $15,000 or less
  • Qualifying farmland is assessed at 30%, not the usual 40%
  • Conservation Use and Forest Land Protection programs value land by its current use and bind you to a 10 or 15 year covenant
  • Historic and brownfield programs use the same January to April filing window

Call 912-632-5614 for the local amounts and what proof to bring. Claiming homestead on a second property anywhere, in or out of Georgia, is unlawful.

Start by getting the numbers. Find out what is owed for each unpaid year, whether a FiFa has been filed, and for a mobile home, whether the April 1 permit tax is current. After that, decide whether to pay now or let the closing agent pay it.

Inherited houses, rentals and vacant properties often carry several unpaid years, and a title search will turn up every recorded lien. Land enrolled in a conservation or forest program needs one more check: ask the assessors what the covenant requires of the next owner, because buyers will want to know.

When you visit Suite 101, bring your deed or parcel number, your latest bill and, if you are already under contract, the signed closing statement. A cash buyer who purchases as-is can close without repairs, though the tax balance is still paid out of your proceeds. Skipping listing, showings and buyer financing also skips weeks of lender appraisal delay, which helps when a bill or lien date is near.

If you sell after the bill is mailed but before it is due, say in the contract who pays it. Get the payoff in writing, keep the receipt, and send the office the closing statement so the record follows the new owner.

faqs.q: What share of market value is taxed in Bacon County?
faqs.a: Assessed value is 40% of fair market value. Exemptions are subtracted from that, and the millage rate, set yearly by the county commissioners and the school board, is applied to what remains.

faqs.q: How can I pay a Bacon County bill?
faqs.a: You can pay in person at Suite 101 in Alma, mail a check postmarked by the deadline, use the drop box, or pay by card online. Call 912-632-5614 with questions.

faqs.q: Does selling split the bill between buyer and seller?
faqs.a: Your closing statement divides it, not the county. If you want any lien recorded against the buyer, deliver the signed statement to Suite 101 within 90 days of the due date.

faqs.q: Is there a refund if I sell in March?
faqs.a: No. The January 1 owner answers for the whole year, and Georgia gives part-year owners no refund.

faqs.q: Who sends the notice of my home's value?
faqs.a: The Board of Tax Assessors, in the same building. Call 912-632-5614, and remember the 45-day appeal clock starts on the notice date.
